Fifth TU reconstruction pilot (after PoleLift, ShipWater, ArrowSignRight, daObjPathLift_c). Two things new here: (1) this TU's real out-of-line D1 (`InvisiblePole::~InvisiblePole(){}`, already real C++ in the legacy source) cannot coexist in the same translation unit with a hand-written mangled-name D0 body -- mwcc hits an internal compiler error (ELFgen.c:483, matching a previously-recorded finding). Fix: delete the D0 body entirely; the real destructor makes the compiler emit D0 itself, and it still MATCHes the ROM. The usual forced `+2` vtable-store addend was still needed on InvisiblePole_Spawn (fourth confirmed occurrence of that fix). (2) This class's OWN compiler-emitted `_ZTI13InvisiblePole`/`_ZTS13InvisiblePole` cannot be schema-fit into `data` with a verified address: the ROM's RTTI embeds the class under a DIFFERENT, coined name (`daBar_c`, per this class's own header comment -- 'daBar_c in the ROM's RTTI... the decomp's own name is kept'), so the cartridge's actual `_ZTS7daBar_c` object is a 7-character string at a size (0xc including padding) that cannot hold the compiler's 13-character 'InvisiblePole' string (0x10) -- not a naming/symbol-table mismatch but a genuine byte-length incompatibility. This is the same class of limitation as [[coined-names-block-data-verification]], now confirmed to block the OWNING class's own RTTI, not just an inherited one. Left unlicensed, deferred to Phase F/attribution work (a non-goal for this pilot series) rather than invented. `_ZTV13InvisiblePole` itself has no such problem (its address point IS configured under this exact name in config/arm9/overlays/ov002/symbols.txt, and every one of its 32 words is a relocation naming a real symbol, not a raw string) but was left out of `data` this round too, for the same reason time was better spent shipping than hand-deriving the storage_alias fields the ov002/daObjAbuku_c precedent used, which needs a named symbol at the 8-byte preamble address that does not exist here.
